anti_generic_signature_read: 'The telescope. It is a real, separate, bored tube on its own plinth and fin, sitting inside the dome and breaking out through the slit - you can see the annular mouth and the bore hole. Combined with sun-versus-moon counters instead of plain red/white discs, that is the one thing that stops this being “a draughts box with a dome on it”.'
blind_action_read: 'signature.png shows the lid coming off: frame 1 closed, with the dome sitting on the box and the edges of the counters showing through a slot around the rim; frame 2 with the dome-and-plate lifted clear and hanging above, exposing the set-up board; frame 3 the open tray alone. So the object does one thing: it opens. The dome lid lifts off vertically to reveal a ready-set 12-a-side draughts game.'
blind_form_read: 'Three stacked volumes. At the bottom, a shallow square tray with plain vertical walls and four L-shaped posts standing up at the corners... Inside it, a flat square board plate... On top, a flat square lid plate of the same footprint. Sitting centrally on that sheet is the dominant mass: a hemispherical dome... standing on a thin skirt/collar ring of slightly larger diameter that gives one crisp reveal line around its foot. The dome is 80% of the plate width... A rectangular trough with a cylinder in it breaks out of the dome's lower flank and projects outward past the silhouette.'
blind_held_read: Unprompted, before knowing anything: 'A small palm-sized draughts set in a lidded tray, where the lid is a model astronomical observatory - a domed roof with a slit and a telescope in it.' It reached 'observatory', 'draughts' and 'the lid lifts off' with no prompting of any kind.
blind_relationship_read: 'The tray carries everything. The board plate lies in the bottom of the tray; the 32 blue tiles are set into it... the counters rest loose on top of the tiles... the lid is held proud of the tray rim, so there is a continuous open slot right around the perimeter through which the outer rank of counters is plainly visible. The dome stands on the lid plate via its skirt ring, dead centre. Inside the dome, a rectangular pedestal block stands on the lid plate at the foot of the slit... the tube rests on the fin and pokes out through the slit.' (It read the two arms as one fin from the oblique frames and corrected itself the moment it measured the plan view, which is exactly the failure mode the brief said the added straight-down frame had to defeat.)
blind_subjects_read: '1 tray/box, grey, with 4 integral corner posts. 1 board plate, pale grey-blue, carrying 32 dark blue chequer tiles... 1 lid plate, teal. 1 dome shell, teal, with 1 slit cut through it. 1 tube (telescope/barrel) with a bored, thick-walled mouth. 1 mount... 24 counters: 12 orange “sun” counters (8 raised blocks in a ring around a central boss) and 12 cream “moon” counters (a single raised crescent).' Shown the doubled pieces with no explanation: 'kings are made by stacking two counters.'

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Asked blind whether the mounted thing was in the middle of the slot or off to one side, on snap/roof/slit-plan-close_el90.png: 'dead centre, not off to one side... a narrow flat strip of identical tone and identical width on both sides'. On snap/roof/slit-plan_el90.png: 'two separate solids inside the slit, 549-572 px and 628-651 px (4.07 mm each), one on each side of the tube, and their centres (560.5 and 639.5) mirror exactly about the slit centre at 600'. Its blind reading of a single fin came from the oblique frames and it withdrew that in full: 'It is a symmetric two-arm yoke. Withdrawn in full; this was the defect being corrected and it is corrected.' Measured on the built part_roof.step at z 18, 25 and 32: -9.000..-5.000 and +5.000..+9.000, within 0.01 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Both arms of the yoke straddle the tube - arm A at x -9.000..-5.000, arm B at +5.000..+9.000 - and the mount is NOT one lone fin beside the tube, nor a one-armed mount carrying the tube off its centreline. This is the exact defect corrected; the archive had them at [-13,-9] and [+1,+5].

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/roof/slit-plan_el90.png: 'the slit walls sit at 515 and 685 px and the arms start at 549 and end at 651, giving 34 px = 6.01 mm of clear air on each side - equal to the pixel, and the air reads as bare plate colour'. And: 'the 6.01 mm is present at every row I sampled from y=780 to y=1025, so the arms are parallel to the walls and never converge on them'. Measured on the built STEP: 6.000 mm both sides.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: There is 6.000 mm of clear air between each arm and its slit wall, EQUAL on both sides of the 30.0 mm slit, and neither arm touches or is hard against a wall.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/roof/slit-plan_el90.png: 'the arms' inner faces are at 572 and 628 px, a gap of 56 px = 9.90 mm, centred at 600.0 px which is the slit's own centreline'. Measured on the built STEP: 10.000 mm, centred on x = 0.000 within 0.01 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: There is a clear gap of 10.000 mm between the two arms, centred on x = 0, the slit's own centreline.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/roof/slit-plan_el90.png and snap/roof/three-quarter_az-135_el28.png: 'the tube overlaps 2.5 mm of each arm's 4.07 mm width - equal both sides - and no parting line appears between tube and arm, so it reads as one fused solid'. Measured: 2.500 mm of overlap per arm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Both arms overlap the tube's own x range (-7.5 .. +7.5) and are fused to it, so the telescope is carried by two arms and not by one.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/roof/slit-plan_el90.png: 'an edge-detection sweep finds every geometric edge with a mirror partner about x=600 within one pixel (0.18 mm) at y=200/300/400/500/600/700/800/900/1000 - dome silhouette, slit walls, both arms, tube, and the arm feet that project past the rim'. Measured by cutting the built part_roof.step against its own mirror image: 0.0000 mm3 of asymmetric volume, against 8987.8055 mm3 (0.9119 % of 985625.9 mm3) for the archive part.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The whole roof is mirror-symmetric about the slit's centre plane, x = 0, and is not lopsided in any way.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Asked blind, before knowing what the object was, 'is the playing surface chequered? point out the squares', on snap/board/populated-plan_el90.png and empty-plan_el90.png: 'Yes, it is an 8 x 8 chequer. There are 32 dark blue tiles in the standard alternating arrangement (4 per rank, offset rank to rank)... perfectly square and perfectly centred on the plate.' Re-read at 1800 px: 'it reads as a chequerboard, and more comfortably than at 1200 - the navy-on-pale alternation is unmistakable at a glance'. At a seated angle, snap/kings/board_az-90_el45.png: 'reads as a chequerboard instantly at a glance with no hunting'. Measured tone: 'RGB (97,111,153) against a (221,229,232) field - a gross colour contrast, not an outline or an engraved step.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The playing surface reads as a chequerboard to an ordinary unprimed viewer, and does NOT depend on a difference a viewer has to hunt for - not a faint outline, not a shallow engraved step.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/board/empty-plan_el90.png: 'sampling all 64 cell centres returns exactly 32 dark cells in perfect alternation, each centred on its cell, with rank 1 reading X.X.X.X. - a1 dark, h1 light', at 'a cell pitch of 178.8 px = 21.95 mm against a plate of 126-1673 px = 190 mm'. Measured on the built part_base.step as a boolean residue against the exact union of 32 chamfered 22.0 mm prisms at the grid centres: 0.000000 mm3.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: There are 32 dark squares, one on each cell where (file + rank) is even, at the cell centres the board grid defines, with a1 dark and h1 light.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/kings/board_az-90_el45.png: 'the tile boundary shows only a 1-2 px tone line and no pocket wall of any height; a 2 mm step would project as ~12.5 px of vertical face at that elevation and scale, and there is nothing remotely like it, so the inlays finish flush'. Also snap/board/inlay-seat_az-60_el22.png. The critic's blind reading of a 0.15 mm pocket was withdrawn: 'it was the parting line between two flush parts of different colour... the correct reading supports flushness rather than undermining it.' Measured: pocket floor z 9.000 + inlay 2.000 = board floor 11.000; flushness error 0.000 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The dark squares are SEPARATE PARTS in a contrasting colour, seated in pockets and finishing FLUSH with the board floor - not proud of it, not sunk below it.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/kings/board_az-90_el45.png and snap/board/empty-plan_el90.png: 'at every tile edge I examined the joint is a plain straight line with no lip, rebate, barb or overhang visible in plan or at 45 degrees.' The baseline's 0.25 mm per side was carried unchanged.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: the inlays have NO retention feature - no clip, lip, undercut, barb or interference. They are gravity-seated only, as the tiled-board baseline requires, and the fit was not tightened toward interference.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/counters/sun-plan_el90.png, sun-oblique_az-90_el22.png, moon-plan_el90.png and moon-oblique_az-90_el22.png, against ref/ref-02 and ref/ref-03. critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: snap/counters/sun-oblique_az-90_el22.png and moon-oblique_az-90_el22.png for relief, sun-plan_el90.png and moon-plan_el90.png for the rings: 'the rim band is flat and horizontal, the sunk field is flat and horizontal, the island's top is flat and horizontal with a vertical cylindrical wall, and every wedge top is flat and horizontal - nowhere is there a dished, conical, domed or curved field. critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE, and deliberately so: the two defects the host scoped out are still present and were NOT fixed - the open perimeter reveal between roof plate and box wall, and the 32 loose gravity-seated inlays. They are recorded together as one disclosed limitation.

largest_risk: The Sun counter's eight wedges do not have the proportions drawn in the commission's own reference art. Measured by the critic at matched disc scale, the reference ray is about 46 x 130 px (aspect 2.8 : 1) against the built part's 75 x 70 px (0.93 : 1); from the source the wedges run radius 4.25 to 6.25, 2.00 mm long and about 2.0 mm wide, aspect 1.0 : 1. At board size the critic reads the result as a cog rather than a sun, and twelve of the twenty-four playing pieces are that counter. This is NOT a change this revision made and it is not repairable here: part_sun_counter.step is byte-identical to the archive (262ccc86f6e4c403...), the archive's own renders of its own counter differ from this revision's by zero pixels, and the brief freezes the sun twice over - by sha256 and in words. Restoring the reference art's proportion would break the byte-identity the same brief requires. The divergence pre-dates this revision by at least one round and is recorded with its numbers in GEOMETRY-NOTES.md C13 for whoever commissions the next one. The critic's second reservation, carried with its positive verdict: in strict side elevation the telescope's housing breaking out of the dome's flank makes the profile read as a teapot, which is the one angle at which the object stops being an observatory. That geometry is frozen too.
resolution: Three rounds, one critic; transcripts in cad/review/revision-c/. Round 1 fully blind: 14 images, nothing else on disk. Unprompted it said 'observatory', 'draughts set', 'the lid lifts off' and 'kings are made by stacking two counters'. Both questions section C required in the FIRST round were put there, on the two frames the brief required added, and both came back correct before anything was revealed: 'dead centre, not off to one side' on the straight-down slit crop, and 'yes, it is an 8 x 8 chequer - 32 dark blue tiles in the standard alternating arrangement' on the whole board. Neither was passed on an oblique frame or a close-up. Of the 15 defects it raised blind it later classified 12 as frozen geometry forbidden to touch and withdrew 3 as its own misreads, including the yoke as a single fin and the pockets as 0.15 mm deep. Its one real finding against this revision's evidence was repaired: board/populated-plan_el90.png duplicated the carried-forward playing/top_el90.png, so both board plan frames were re-rendered at 1800 px. NO GEOMETRY CHANGED - the part STEPs, snap/iso.png and snap/signature.png are byte-identical to those read blind - and it re-read them. Round 2 revealed the brief and took 19 requirements separately; two returned FAILS and it showed they contradicted each other. Both were the Manager's paraphrase of the archive's prose, not requirements the brief contains, since the brief freezes the counters by sha256 rather than describing them; both were restated and re-put. Round 3 resolved its one blocking claim, that the sun's wedges were reproportioned. Given the hashes and the archive's own renders, and told a persisting FAILS would be sealed as blocking, it verified them itself ('max pixel difference 0, differing pixels 0') and restated it as a pre-existing divergence between the frozen part and the reference art. Desirability moved from no to yes on its own reasoning, with two reservations on frozen geometry kept in largest_risk.
reviewer: one independent native critic, blind to the Wish, brief and product identity for all of round 1 and told to read nothing but the 14 images. Rounds 2-3 primed. See cad/review/revision-c/.
